findings.problem: +264 kJ comes from 611 − 347 (only the carbon–carbon change). The feedback restates the whole setup instead of naming the mistake.
findings.new_text: This counts only the change from C=C to C–C. The Cl–Cl bond broken and the two C–Cl bonds formed also count.

findings.problem: −527 kJ comes from 243 − 770 (the broken C–H is left out). The feedback restates the setup instead of naming the mistake.
findings.new_text: This forgets that one C–H bond in methane is broken so the Cl can attach.

findings.problem: Adding the two sums gives +1541 kJ, but the distractor is −1541 kJ, so the feedback does not quite describe how the pick arises.
findings.new_text: This adds the bonds broken and the bonds formed together. The bonds formed must be subtracted from the bonds broken.

findings.problem: +922 kJ comes from 1856 − (436 + 498), forming only one H–H. The feedback restates the setup instead of naming the mistake.
findings.new_text: This forms only one H–H bond. The reaction makes two H₂ molecules, so two H–H bonds form.

findings.problem: "The sign is wrong." does not help the student see where the sign slipped.
findings.new_text: Check the rearrangement. The products together are more negative than ΔH°rxn, so ethanol's ΔH°f must come out negative.

findings.problem: 4.91×10⁻³⁶ J comes from h ÷ (cλ). The feedback only restates the formula and does not name the slip.
findings.new_text: This divides h by both c and λ. The speed of light goes on top, multiplied by h.

findings.problem: 4.73×10²⁸ comes from using hc × λ as the photon energy. The student did divide by an energy per photon, so the second sentence does not point at the real slip.
findings.new_text: This multiplies hc by λ when finding the photon energy. The energy of one photon is hc divided by λ.

findings.problem: 1.77×10² s⁻¹ comes from c × λ. The feedback restates the formula without naming the slip.
findings.new_text: This multiplies c by λ. Frequency comes from dividing c by λ.

findings.problem: 247 nm is half the keyed wavelength, so it comes from twice the energy per bond. The feedback does not name that slip.
findings.new_text: This uses twice the energy needed. One photon only has to break one Cl–Cl bond, so do not double the bond energy.

findings.problem: The hint gives the full setup with the numbers plugged in (2.179×10⁻¹⁸ J × (1/1² − 1/3²)).
findings.new_text: Find the energy difference between the n = 3 and n = 1 levels from the En equation. Then use λ = hc/ΔE.

findings.problem: Stating the 288 nm threshold gives away the answer, since only one choice is shorter than 288 nm.
findings.new_text: 312 nm is longer than the threshold wavelength, so its photons carry too little energy. Find the threshold wavelength from c ÷ ν.
